# Gallivant import capabilities (doc/gallivant/caps.md): the compiler
# enforces the capability grants on imports ("with [...]") at module
# boundaries, using the effective capability set each package records in
# its export data.

[short] skip 'compiles several modules'

# cmd/go passes the module path of the package being compiled to the
# compiler, but not when compiling the standard library.
go build -n -a -o $devnull ./ok
stderr 'compile.* -p main .*-modpath=example\.com/app'
stderr 'compile.* -p fmt .* -std'
! stderr 'compile.* -p fmt .*-modpath'

# A dependency from another module that uses more capabilities than its
# import is granted fails to compile. The diagnostic shows the full
# required set and where each missing capability originates, including
# capabilities inherited transitively from the dependency's own imports.
! go build -o $devnull ./bad
stderr '^(\./)?bad[/\\]main\.go:7:2: import "example\.com/dep" uses capabilities \[file\.write, net\] but is only granted \[file\.write\]$'
stderr '^\t\[net\] example\.com/dep/dep\.go:6: import "example\.com/dep2"$'
stderr '^\t\[net\] example\.com/dep2/dep2\.go:6: net\.Dial$'
! stderr '^\t\[file\.write\]'

# Granting the full set fixes it. Standard-library imports and imports of
# packages in the same module (even ones that read the environment) need
# no grant.
go build -o $devnull ./ok
go vet ./ok

# Only packages of main modules are checked. example.com/dep3 imports
# example.com/dep2 without a grant, which is fine because dep3 is a
# dependency; dep2's net capability is charged to our grant on dep3.
go build -o $devnull ./viadep3
go build -n -a -o $devnull ./viadep3
stderr 'compile.* -p main .*-checkcaps'
! stderr 'compile.* -p example\.com/dep3 .*-checkcaps'
! go build -o $devnull ./viadep3bad
stderr '^(\./)?viadep3bad[/\\]main\.go:3:8: import "example\.com/dep3" uses capabilities \[net\] but is only granted \[\]$'

# Grants are enforced by default; "caps false" in go.mod opts a module
# written before grants existed out. Its capability facts are still
# recorded.
go list -m -f '{{.Caps}}'
stdout '^true$'
cd legacy
go list -m -f '{{.Caps}}'
stdout '^false$'
go build -o $devnull .
go build -n -a -o $devnull .
! stderr 'compile.* -p main .*-checkcaps'
cd ../badcaps
! go list -m
stderr 'go\.mod:4: usage: caps \[true\|false\]'
cd ..

# Unknown capabilities are rejected.
! go build -o $devnull ./badtoken
stderr '^(\./)?badtoken[/\\]main\.go:7:43: unknown capability bogus \(want one of \[.*\]\)$'

# A grant is a bracketed list.
! go build -o $devnull ./unbracketed
stderr '^(\./)?unbracketed[/\\]main\.go:6:25: expected ''\['', found net$'

-- go.mod --
module example.com/app

go 1.27

require (
	example.com/dep v0.0.0
	example.com/dep2 v0.0.0
	example.com/dep3 v0.0.0
)

replace example.com/dep => ./dep

replace example.com/dep2 => ./dep2

replace example.com/dep3 => ./dep3
-- viadep3/main.go --
package main

import "example.com/dep3" with [net]

func main() { dep3.Ping() }
-- viadep3bad/main.go --
package main

import "example.com/dep3"

func main() { dep3.Ping() }
-- dep3/go.mod --
module example.com/dep3

go 1.27

require example.com/dep2 v0.0.0

replace example.com/dep2 => ../dep2
-- dep3/dep3.go --
package dep3

import "example.com/dep2"

func Ping() { dep2.Ping() }
-- internal/helper/helper.go --
package helper

import "os"

func Home() string { return os.Getenv("HOME") }
-- bad/main.go --
package main

import (
	"fmt"

	"example.com/app/internal/helper"
	"example.com/dep" with [file.write]
)

func main() {
	fmt.Println(helper.Home(), dep.Save("x"))
}
-- ok/main.go --
package main

import (
	"fmt"

	"example.com/app/internal/helper"
	"example.com/dep" with [file.write, net]
)

func main() {
	fmt.Println(helper.Home(), dep.Save("x"))
}
-- badtoken/main.go --
package main

import (
	"fmt"

	"example.com/app/internal/helper"
	"example.com/dep" with [file.write, net, bogus]
)

func main() {
	fmt.Println(helper.Home(), dep.Save("x"))
}
-- unbracketed/main.go --
package main

import (
	"fmt"

	"example.com/dep" with net
)

func main() {
	fmt.Println(dep.Save("x"))
}
-- dep/go.mod --
module example.com/dep

go 1.27

require example.com/dep2 v0.0.0

replace example.com/dep2 => ../dep2
-- dep/dep.go --
package dep

import (
	"os"

	"example.com/dep2" with [net]
)

func Save(s string) error {
	dep2.Ping()
	return os.WriteFile("/tmp/x", []byte(s), 0o644)
}
-- dep2/go.mod --
module example.com/dep2

go 1.27
-- dep2/dep2.go --
package dep2

import "net"

func Ping() {
	c, err := net.Dial("tcp", "localhost:1")
	if err == nil {
		c.Close()
	}
}
-- legacy/go.mod --
module example.com/legacy

go 1.27
caps false

require example.com/dep2 v0.0.0

replace example.com/dep2 => ../dep2
-- legacy/main.go --
package main

import "example.com/dep2"

func main() { dep2.Ping() }
-- badcaps/go.mod --
module example.com/badcaps

go 1.27
caps maybe
